transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. __. What brings you in today?

Um... hi. I guess I'm just here because... I'm having a hard time keeping things organized. 

Between my schoolwork and... I have this little accessories shop. It just feels like my supplies, the due dates, receipts, assignment notes... they all just end up in piles everywhere. I never really know what to do first.
Do you often find it hard to stay focused on a task or conversation?

Um... yeah, I guess. Like... if I'm in class, or watching a video for my assignments. I'll start out listening fine, but... after a few minutes, my mind just sort of wanders off to charm designs, or... order ideas. And then I realize I missed half of what was actually said. So... yeah.
Did you have similar trouble with focus or organization when you were a child?

Um... yeah, I think so. My mom actually still has some old notes from my teachers in elementary school. Um... they mostly just said things like... I was always getting out of my seat. Or, you know, talking before I was called on. And... I guess I rushed through group activities a lot, even when I knew how to do the work. So... yeah.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?
Um... no, not really. I mean... I don't think I worry more than anyone else. Just... normal things, I guess.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a clear lifelong pattern of inattention and hyperactive/impulsive behaviors beginning in childhood, with current functional difficulty in schoolwork and managing a business. Symptoms include poor organization, distractibility, mind-wandering, leaving seat, blurting out, and rushing through tasks. Anxiety-related excessive worry was denied, supporting ADHD rather than an anxiety disorder.
